application_credentials.description:
Follow the [instructions]({more_info_url}) for [OAuth consent screen]({oauth_consent_url}) to give Home Assistant access to your Google Calendar. You also need to create Application Credentials linked to your account:
1. Go to [Credentials]({oauth_creds_url}) and select **Create Credentials**.
1. From the drop-down list select **OAuth client ID**.
1. Select **Web application** for the Application Type.

unnamed_colours.title: Colours without a name
unnamed_colours.description:
These calendars use colours that have no name in Google Calendar:

{colours}

If you split now, these colours get calendar entities named after the colour, such as `calendar.family_radicchio`. Naming the colour later renames the entity, but its entity ID stays the same.

To name a colour: in Google Calendar on the web, open one of the events above, open the colour menu and select the pencil next to the colour. Then come back here to split the calendar.

not_split.title: Calendar not split
not_split.description:
**{calendars}** won't be split for now.

To split it later: name its colours in Google Calendar (on the web, open an event, open the colour menu and select the pencil next to the colour), then open **Configure** again and tick it.

Select **Submit** to save the rest of your choices.

unnamed_colours.title: {calendar}: colours without a name
unnamed_colours.description:
The **{calendar}** calendar is split by event colour, and these colours have no name in Google Calendar, so their calendar entities are named after the colour:

{colours}

To name a colour: in Google Calendar on the web, open one of the events above, open the colour menu and select the pencil next to the colour. Then reload the Google Calendar integration. The entity is renamed; its entity ID stays the same, and you can change it in the entity's settings.

If you're happy with the colour names, ignore this. It comes back if another colour without a name starts being used.
